**Impacted CIs are not yet available on this dashboard.** Deriving them needs the CMDB relationship graph, which lives in `cmdb-ci-relations-000002` (33.9M edges: `parent`, `child`, `type.name`, and an `impacted_ci` field naming which side is downstream). Incidents with no CI on the record now appear in *Impacted Domain* under **⚠️ No CI mapped**, so the P1 and P2 columns of that panel add up to the tiles exactly. The *Affected CIs* table still lists only incidents that have a CI, so its row count equals the tile total minus the *No CI mapped* row.

*Affected CIs is one row per incident × CI.* The source is a snapshot index, so an incident that was reassigned or re-described inside the dashboard window used to appear on more than one row. The query now groups on `number`, `ci.name` and `priority` only, and collapses the descriptive columns with `VALUES(...)` + `MV_MAX(...)`, so each incident contributes exactly one row per CI. For remotely-collected tiers — vSphere, GCP, Kubernetes, Oracle, IBM MQ, Prometheus — `host.name` is the **collector** running the integration, not the device (e.g. `vsphere.virtualmachine` carries 150k documents under a single `host.name`).
